organization.name: Dedaub
organization.summary: Smart contract security company. Its GitHub organization Dedaub was created 2019-10-28. Its products named in the proposal are a monitoring platform, a CLI and the Gigahorse-based decompiler.

previousFunding.label: TheDAO Security Fund Round 1 record: Dedaub Decompiler: From Bytecode to Solidity-Like Code

delivery.grant: TheDAO Security Fund Round 1: Dedaub Decompiler: From Bytecode to Solidity-Like Code
delivery.promised: Per Dedaub's own post, the grant funded more accurate and readable Solidity-like decompiler output and a larger free allowance for AI-powered reconstruction. The Round 1 record lists payments and no deliverables.

sources.label: Dedaub blog post (self-reported by the grantee, dated 2026-09-07)

claims.claim: The CLI and agent skill are MIT licensed with reference notes for 95 protocols.
claims.method: GitHub API: MIT, created 2026-05-25, last push 2026-11-25. The references/protocols folder holds 164 subfolders, not 95, so the count differs from the proposal. The counting basis of the proposal is unknown, and no contradiction is asserted.

claims.claim: The monitoring platform at app.dedaub.com is live on 8 EVM chains.
claims.method: The app URL returned HTTP 403 to an automated request. Live status and chain count could not be confirmed.

claims.claim: The Gigahorse decompiler has been free since 2018 with more than 16,000 registered users across ten EVM chains.
claims.method: The Dedaub post states the engine has run since September 2018 with more than 12,000 registered users across nine EVM chains. The proposal figures are higher and may be later. Not verified: user, request and subscriber counts come from the applicant's own pages; no independent public source was found.
